title: One shot prompt VS game design phase document
author: Ill-Past4609
selftext: So I’ve tried one shot prompts and game design document with phases that doesn’t allow me to continue adding new features until i test and approve everything is working what do you think is best ? And when it comes to final game as far as Art/UI/ animation do you guys do that as you prompt or finalice in the end because I’m currently stuck with a simple square shapes etc but every core loop works to the letter! Mining , crafting etc

comments.author: Snoo-29395
comments.body:
Nothing good can come up with one shootting a game.

I'm 4 months into my game and i barely scratched the surface.

\- Think about what you want and create a good GDD. Stick to it, you can change it but try not changing the scope and the main pillars of it while developing

\- Define a MVP for a vertical slice you can actually ship as a demo

\- Split the work into milestones

\- Split each milestone into subtickets, the smaller the better

\- Plan each ticket at once, once the plan makes sense to you, just then work on it

\- Repeat

replies.author: Ill-Past4609
replies.body: That’s exactly where I Am at the moment been 2 days and still phase 1 lol because codex wants me to test every core loop lol and then i always report any errors glitches etc. now what about art/ui/ menu etc do you do that as you go or at the end ??

replies.author: Snoo-29395
replies.body:
The most important thing is to test if the game is fun, so i bascially modeled a graybox, and once i make sure i was actually having a good time testing it, moved to the juice.

In my case i use royalty free assets and make the animations on my own

comments.author: ScutFarkush
comments.body: I am about 9 months into my game and i am at the point where I feel like I am 80% done and still have 80% to go. Should have my steam page set up this next week and I will be marketing hard after that while doing polishing balancing and finding playtesters. It was a lot of work to get it to where it is, to make it not look or feel ai. I do not like things looking ai, it generally means they were 1 shot. I start new sessions often, I have different sessions for graphics, gameplay, ui, progression, sounds, music, code reviews, play testing bots, i have build mcp servers, shaders, consistency etc. AI game dev is still a lot of work, but i finally have built an idea i have had for about 4 years now and it is coming out exactly how i wanted it.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
Ai live and die by context. The issue with one prompting is that Ai will now have a working game in-context. You will end up wasting time steering ai away from it i.e. "no. This and that is for the previous demo only etc"

Granted, astra/fable are smarter and they can possibly navigate the situation 

I still prefer doing things in phases. Seem less confusing for AI imo

comments.author: Fairway3Games
comments.body:
Here's the thing: even the BEST one-shot game is unlikely to be a reasonable game.  It might have bits and pieces that resemble other games, but it's often an amalgamation of very 'thin' features.  It seems 'cohesive' only in the sense that the AI made a bunch of decisions and was able to string them together.

But once you start trying to convert it to something it wasn't built for, you end up unwinding the string that tied it together.

Try to add features. Try to refine interactions. Try to add effects or game play mechanisms.  All of those things you try to back fill, you're almost better off not having one-shot anything at all.
